title: Visible From the Right
statement:
Imagine standing to the **right** of a binary tree and looking at it. At every level you can see only the node that is farthest to the right on that level; the others are hidden behind it.

Return the values you can see, from the top level to the bottom level. A node deeper on the left can still be visible if the right side has no node at that depth.

examples.explanation: Level 0: 1. Level 1: 2 and 3, you see 3. Level 2: 5 and 4, you see 4.
There is nothing on the right at any level, so the left nodes are visible.

hints.nudge: You only need ONE node per level. If you look at the right child before the left child, which node do you meet first on each level?
hints.pattern: Depth-first search that visits the right child first and records a value the first time it reaches a new depth (or a level-by-level search that keeps the last node of each level).
hints.pseudocode:
result = empty list
visit(node, depth):
  if node is missing: return
  if depth == size of result: append node.val
  visit(node.right, depth + 1)
  visit(node.left, depth + 1)
visit(root, 0)
return result
hints.walkthrough: Two ways work. Level by level: use a queue, process one whole level at a time, and keep the last node of each level. Or with recursion: visit the RIGHT child before the LEFT child and carry the current depth. The first time you reach a depth you have not seen yet (depth equals the size of the result so far), the node you are standing on is the right-most node of that level, because everything to its right was visited earlier and did not reach that depth. Append its value. Left nodes only get recorded for depths the right side did not reach. Each node is visited once: O(n).
